title: Lowest Common Ancestor in Binary Tree
question: How would you find the Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) of two target nodes p and q in a Binary Tree (not necessarily a Binary Search Tree)?

rubric.name: problem_clarification
rubric.description: Clarifies node guarantees (are p and q guaranteed to exist?), tree structure, and node parent pointer existence.

rubric.name: algorithmic_reasoning
rubric.description: Explains post-order DFS traversal returning non-null when target is found and returning current node when both subtrees match.

rubric.name: time_space_complexity
rubric.description: Derives O(N) time complexity for visiting tree nodes and O(H) space complexity for call stack (H=height).

rubric.name: edge_case_handling
rubric.description: Handles case where p is ancestor of q, single-node tree, or targets at opposite tree ends.

rubric.name: communication_clarity
rubric.description: Walks through recursive return values clearly.

expected_signals: Uses recursive DFS post-order traversal to bubble up found targets
Explains why LCA is reached when left and right subtree calls both return non-null
Correctly notes O(H) recursion stack space, bounded by O(N) in skewed tree
red_flags: Assumes tree is a BST and attempts value comparison `p.val < root.val` without checking tree type
Stores entire root-to-node paths unnecessarily without recognizing O(1) extra space post-order optimization
Fails to handle when target node is ancestor of the other
follow_up_prompts: How would your algorithm simplify if the tree was guaranteed to be a Binary Search Tree (BST)?
What if each node had a pointer to its parent node? How would you solve it then?
